newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta slips further against mark in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Peseta slips further against mark in late trade.

text.p: The peseta weakened further against the mark in late trade on Friday and traders said it could slip further if bonds continued to fall.
By 1645 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.30/32 per mark, compared with late Thursday's levels of around 84.06/09.

"We would normally expect the peseta to return to levels close to 83.90/84.00 per mark, but it's still a bit premature to say, and if the funds continue to flow out of bonds, the peseta could continue to fall," said one trader.
While bonds and equities tumbled during Friday to end lower, many dealers said they expected the correction to last only a short time.
Traders said they had not seen the central bank checking rates or intervening for the last couple of days.
"The Bank of Spain is letting the market find its own value at the moment," said one trader.
Against the dollar, the peseta was trading at 137.20/25 late on Friday, compared with levels late on Thursday of around 137.80/90.
